<reason>PRO's burden-shift case survived: silence should end broad coercion, not preserve it. CON's privileged-revocation alternative was inventive, but PRO showed it still forces opponents to assemble a majority against a sitting executive mid-crisis, while sunset forces the power-holder to earn continuation. CON's midnight hostage-taking and lapse risks were serious, yet PRO's weighing—a loud, repairable lapse versus quiet, indefinite drift—was cleaner and less neutralized.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's Rebuttal 2 resolved the alleged procedural contradiction: if legislatures can fast-track revocation, they can fast-track renewal, and if neither is reliable the default should favor liberty over decree. CON's procedural-versus-substantive extortion reply narrowed but did not eliminate that burden asymmetry.</best_rebuttal>
